title: Discounted preservation water rate for habitat restoration
summary: On Sept. 5, the committee voted to use the administration's revised Bill 99, which sets a "preservation rate" for native species habitat, and approved a change to match the agricultural rates, with eight ayes. The rate was first proposed at $4.98 per 1,000 gallons, against an $8.34 general rate and about $7 delivery cost. The water director said a lower rate would barely affect revenue.

timeline.text: The sponsor said Bill 99 sets that rate in the budget.
Pass Bill 56 CD1 on second and final reading: Bill 56 CD1, allowing discounted water rates for habitat restoration, passed second and final reading.
A council member said it was unanimously supported in committee.
A council member said the Water Department proposed the bill.
The council passed Committee Report 25-46 on first reading with seven ayes.
A committee recommended Bill 56, which would discount water rates for customers using water to conserve or restore native Hawaiian species habitat.
